fieldMarks: Brown back overlain with greenish grey, pale gold or reddish hues and sprinkled with brassy specks, mostly on snout, shoulders and upper tail base.
Dusky grey belly; expanded toes with squared tips; rounded prehensile tail; 16-17 costal grooves.
Adult males have triangular heads from strong jaw muscles; females are slightly longer (max about 65 mm snout-vent).
Young are dark brown with a brassy stripe from neck to tail tip and a brassy triangle on the head.
behavior: Usually found singly under bark, in decaying stumps and logs, and in cliff cracks; partly arboreal.
Inactive in cold and hot, dry weather; may gather in moist decayed logs in dry summers.
Carnivorous on invertebrates; males often bear fight scars.
habitat: Mesic coniferous forest (Douglas-fir, redwood, hemlock, Port Orford cedar), especially forest edges, clearings and burned areas.
Uses large, mid-decay logs with sloughing bark.
range: Coastal forests of Oregon and northern California, from the Columbia River south, plus a separate group on Vancouver Island and adjacent islands in British Columbia; sea level to about 1,500-1,700 m.
